findings.title: Author-authorization cannot adopt the required base-checker route within the proposed GREEN scope
findings.evidence: The active author workflow directly executes the candidate root checker without an explicit base at `.github/workflows/protocol-v3-author-authorization.yml:30`, contrary to the proposal's merge-base-checker/no-candidate-fallback rule. Changing that workflow also changes bytes which this active supplement checker requires to match its policy hash at lines 95–96. The proposal calls the workflow already routed at `red-proposal.md:59` but does not include the author-authorization policy/checker in the GREEN disposition. Left as written, either this consumer remains self-blessable or its supplement check fails. Add the workflow and author-authorization policy to the exact amendment roster; route through the unique merge-base root checker with an explicit base and bound root, repin the workflow in the supplement policy, and extend its routing analyzer/mutations accordingly while retaining the author checker and v2 command.
findings.violated_requirement: Full active consumer coverage; base-governed authority with no candidate fallback; preserved subsystem custody and commands.

findings.title: The supersession map omits active root-conformance tests that still bind historical hashes to live files
findings.evidence: This test hashes every `acceptedInputs` path against its historical digest; its contract pins the live registry and schema to the obsolete hashes at `tests/fixtures/phase-n1prime-c2/independent-reference-vector-contract.json:26–32`. It remains an accepted current test at `tests/fixtures/phase-n1prime-e4/root-test-lifecycle-contract.json:49`. The same live-file conflation occurs in regenerated-reference tests at `tests/protocol-v3-regenerated-reference-n1prime-d.test.ts:571–574` and `tests/protocol-v3-regenerated-reference-remediation-n1prime-d2.test.ts:602–604`, also selected at lifecycle lines 51–52. The proposal explicitly maps e/e2/e3/e4 and successor tests but not these consumers. Freeze an exact disposition for c2/d/d2: preserve historical statements and semantic controls, stop asserting their old registry/schema hashes against current paths, retitle superseded predicates, and assign current schema/present-field identity solely to the new current contract without skipping these suites.
findings.violated_requirement: Full active consumer coverage and honest historical-test supersession without relabeling old evidence.

findings.title: The source-bearing semantic-validation seam is not freeze-complete
findings.evidence: The retained snapshot envelope has a hash-only `files` map and only one `workflow` source, matching `makeSnapshot` at `packages/protocol-v3/scripts/check-protocol-v3-freeze.mjs:923–970`. The new contract nevertheless requires semantic schema mutations and routing validation across the schema, oracle, and all active workflows. Lines 142–143 and 156–158 defer any new content-bearing field/export, manifest roster, consumer mapping, and command selection. Without freezing that boundary, RED can accidentally demonstrate only stale-hash refusal or fail on an invented export. Specify before RED either a hash-bound source map for every semantically parsed artifact or an exact CLI/source-reader plus directly callable validator API, including how each source is tied to `files`; then freeze the complete manifest and mutation harness.
findings.violated_requirement: Implementable exact RED seam, semantic-validator adequacy, workflow-routing mutation evidence, and mutation-baseline independence.

checked_requirements: Prospective-baseline trust reset: the proposed trust model is sound in principle. It removes bootstrap authority, rejects old/missing/malformed bases, requires exactly one merge base, runs the merge-base checker with an explicitly bound root, and forbids candidate fallback. Base policy and inventory govern candidate bytes, preserving anti-self-blessing.

The signed reviewed baseline is honestly described as an out-of-band prospective trust-anchor amendment, not an old-policy-approved PR. Current/current integrity is explicitly disclaimed as transition evidence. Host branch protection is neither changed nor claimed verified. This is not itself a hidden security contradiction, but installation on a protected branch remains external operational work.
One-current-contract constraint: no dual registry, historical-tree projection, accept-either hash, recursive custody chain, or relabeling of historical sign-offs is proposed.

Registry/runtime scope: registry bytes remain unchanged; the optional multiplier remains optional; schema boundaries 1 through 1,000,000 do not widen Node's supported profile digests or alter live-journal's separate boundary.
Schema direction is correct: add the optional property with integer bounds and matching native metadata, retain the seven required fields and closed-object behavior, and do not inject a default.

Independent oracle design is adequate in direction: it is bounded to the actual ASCII/nonnegative-integer parameter corpus, independently implements canonical key ordering/varuint/zigzag/framing, uses Node SHA-256 rather than production helpers, and requires reviewed literal absent/present-four bytes and digests plus domain/drop/default mutants.

True causal RED is available through the existing exported `evaluateProtocolV3Freeze({ base, current })` seam at `packages/protocol-v3/scripts/check-protocol-v3-freeze.mjs:842`; its stale immutable registry/schema closure provides a real contract failure rather than a missing export or unsupported flag.

Mutation-baseline independence is explicitly required: each mutation family starts from the same known-good current baseline and coordinated artifact/policy/checker edits are evaluated by independent base authority.

Seal, pacemaker, successor-routed workflows, journal, anchor, blueprint, gossip, CODEOWNERS, ordinary-test lifecycle, v2 separation, and historical governance suites were inspected for the cited custody and supersession obligations.

Existing historical references, locks, vectors, formal sign-offs, and successor evidence can remain preserved while their obsolete live-routing/current-byte assertions are superseded; their safety obligations need replacement, not continued ownership.
limitations: No tests, checkers, project code, builds, compilers, formatters, network access, Git mutations, writes, or other models were run, as required.
The eight dirty production owners were treated as inherited, preserved, and out of review.

The proposal is not eligible for implementation release until the three findings are resolved and the exact protected manifest, source-validation interface, consumer replacement table, command roster, and absent/present-four oracle literals are frozen and independently reviewed.
Repository evidence cannot establish branch-protection configuration or prove how the signed replacement baseline will be installed on a protected host branch.
